\chapter{Honours and Winners}
\label{ch:ml-honours-and-winners}
\hlchaptermodality{396}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can say an award, an honour, a winner, to honour and to make one's own.}

Complete the last lesson of chapter 396: I can say an award, an honour, a winner, to honour and to make one's own.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{പുരസ്കാരം} (puraskāraṁ)}{പുരസ്കാരം (puraskāraṁ)}]{\ml{പുരസ്കാരം} (puraskāraṁ) — an award}

\label{lesson:ML-C396-puraskaram}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for an origin, then the Malayalam for a grandmother's tale.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{പുരസ്കാരം}}
\textbf{\ml{പുരസ്കാരം}} — \emph{puraskāraṁ} — \textquotedblleft{}an award\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{ആ} \ml{ഗായകന്} \ml{ഒരു} \ml{വലിയ} \ml{പുരസ്കാരം} \ml{കിട്ടി}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ā gāyakanŭ oru valiya puraskāraṁ kiṭṭi.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
That singer got a big award.
\end{quote}

A formal word; \ml{സമ്മാനം} is the everyday prize.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{പുരസ്കാരം}} (\emph{puraskāraṁ}) is borrowed from Sanskrit \emph{puraskāra}, \textquotedblleft{}placing in front, honouring, distinction\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{puraskāraṁ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{puraskāraṁ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ā gāyakanŭ oru valiya puraskāraṁ kiṭṭi.} — That singer got a big award.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for an origin, then the Malayalam for a grandmother's tale, then say \emph{puraskāraṁ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{പുരസ്കാരം} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}An award\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{ബഹുമതി} (bahumati)}{ബഹുമതി (bahumati)}]{\ml{ബഹുമതി} (bahumati) — an honour}

\label{lesson:ML-C396-bahumati}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for a grandmother's tale, then the Malayalam for an award.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{ബഹുമതി}}
\textbf{\ml{ബഹുമതി}} — \emph{bahumati} — \textquotedblleft{}an honour\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{അത്} \ml{ഞങ്ങൾക്ക്} \ml{ഒരു} \ml{വലിയ} \ml{ബഹുമതി} \ml{ആണ്}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{atŭ ñaṅṅaḷkkŭ oru valiya bahumati āṇŭ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
That is a great honour for us.
\end{quote}

Also a title or a decoration given by a government.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{ബഹുമതി}} (\emph{bahumati}) is borrowed from Sanskrit \emph{bahumati}, \textquotedblleft{}high opinion, esteem\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams), from \emph{bahu}, \textquotedblleft{}much\textquotedblright{}, and \emph{mati}, \textquotedblleft{}thought\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bahumati}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bahumati}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{atŭ ñaṅṅaḷkkŭ oru valiya bahumati āṇŭ.} — That is a great honour for us.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for a grandmother's tale, then the Malayalam for an award, then say \emph{bahumati} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{ബഹുമതി} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}An honour\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{ജേതാവ്} (jētāvŭ)}{ജേതാവ് (jētāvŭ)}]{\ml{ജേതാവ്} (jētāvŭ) — a winner}

\label{lesson:ML-C396-jetavu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for an award, then the Malayalam for an honour.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{ജേതാവ്}}
\textbf{\ml{ജേതാവ്}} — \emph{jētāvŭ} — \textquotedblleft{}a winner\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{മത്സരത്തിലെ} \ml{ജേതാവിന്} \ml{പ്രിൻസിപ്പൽ} \ml{സമ്മാനം} \ml{നൽകി}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{matsarattile jētāvinŭ prinsippal sammānaṁ nalki.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The principal gave the prize to the winner of the competition.
\end{quote}

Plural \ml{ജേതാക്കൾ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{ജേതാവ്}} (\emph{jētāvŭ}) is borrowed from Sanskrit \emph{jetṛ}, \textquotedblleft{}victorious; a conqueror\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams). Sanskrit nouns in -tṛ come into Malayalam in -\ml{താവ്}, as in \ml{ശ്രോതാവ്}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jētāvŭ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jētāvŭ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{matsarattile jētāvinŭ prinsippal sammānaṁ nalki.} — The principal gave the prize to the winner of the competition.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for an award, then the Malayalam for an honour, then say \emph{jētāvŭ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{ജേതാവ്} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A winner\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{ആദരിക്കുക} (ādarikkuka)}{ആദരിക്കുക (ādarikkuka)}]{\ml{ആദരിക്കുക} (ādarikkuka) — to honour}

\label{lesson:ML-C396-adarikkuka}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for an honour, then the Malayalam for a winner.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{ആദരിക്കുക}}
\textbf{\ml{ആദരിക്കുക}} — \emph{ādarikkuka} — \textquotedblleft{}to honour\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{പള്ളിക്കൂടം} \ml{പഴയ} \ml{അധ്യാപകരെ} \ml{ആദരിച്ചു}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{paḷḷikkūṭaṁ paḻaya adhyāpakare ādariccu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The school honoured its old teachers.
\end{quote}

Past: \ml{ആദരിച്ചു}, \emph{ādariccu}.

The person honoured takes -\ml{എ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{ആദരിക്കുക}} (\emph{ādarikkuka}) is built from Sanskrit \emph{ādara}, \textquotedblleft{}respect\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 1142), with the Malayalam verb ending -\ml{ിക്കുക}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ādarikkuka}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ādarikkuka}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{paḷḷikkūṭaṁ paḻaya adhyāpakare ādariccu.} — The school honoured its old teachers.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for an honour, then the Malayalam for a winner, then say \emph{ādarikkuka} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{ആദരിക്കുക} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To honour\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{സ്വന്തമാക്കുക} (svantamākkuka)}{സ്വന്തമാക്കുക (svantamākkuka)}]{\ml{സ്വന്തമാക്കുക} (svantamākkuka) — to make one's own; to win}

\label{lesson:ML-C396-svantamakkuka}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for a winner, then the Malayalam for to honour.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{സ്വന്തമാക്കുക}}
\textbf{\ml{സ്വന്തമാക്കുക}} — \emph{svantamākkuka} — \textquotedblleft{}to make one's own; to win\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{ഞങ്ങളുടെ} \ml{ടീം} \ml{കപ്പ്} \ml{സ്വന്തമാക്കി}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ñaṅṅaḷuṭe ṭīṁ kappŭ svantamākki.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Our team won the cup.
\end{quote}

Past: \ml{സ്വന്തമാക്കി}, \emph{svantamākki}.

\ml{സ്വന്തം}, one's own, + \ml{ആക്കുക}, to make: to buy, win or take something as yours.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{സ്വന്തമാക്കുക}} (\emph{svantamākkuka}) joins \ml{സ്വന്തം}, \textquotedblleft{}one's own\textquotedblright{}, usually traced to Sanskrit \emph{sva}, \textquotedblleft{}self, own\textquotedblright{}, and \ml{ആക്കുക}, \textquotedblleft{}to make\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{svantamākkuka}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{svantamākkuka}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ñaṅṅaḷuṭe ṭīṁ kappŭ svantamākki.} — Our team won the cup.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for a winner, then the Malayalam for to honour, then say \emph{svantamākkuka} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{സ്വന്തമാക്കുക} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To make one's own; to win\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[(dialogue)]{Words from chapters 389–396 — a review}

\label{lesson:ML-R396-review-389-396}



\begin{quote}
Say the Malayalam for a housewarming and a naming ceremony.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item a housewarming, a naming ceremony, a honeymoon, to settle, to migrate
  \item a send-off, to bid farewell, to see off, to say goodbye, to leave one's homeland
  \item a funeral, a cremation ground, a coffin, to cremate, to bury
  \item condolence, a tribute, a death anniversary, a cemetery, to offer condolences
  \item a commemoration, a memorial, a statue, a stone inscription, to commemorate
  \item property, an heir, a will, a widow, heritage
  \item an ancestor, a successor, a custom, an origin, a grandmother's tale
  \item an award, an honour, a winner, to honour, to make one's own
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
A housewarming? (\textbf{\ml{ഗൃഹപ്രവേശം}}, \emph{gṛhapravēśaṁ}.) A naming ceremony? (\textbf{\ml{നാമകരണം}}, \emph{nāmakaraṇaṁ}.) A honeymoon? (\textbf{\ml{മധുവിധു}}, \emph{madhuvidhu}.) To settle? (\textbf{\ml{താമസമാക്കുക}}, \emph{tāmasamākkuka}.) To migrate? (\textbf{\ml{കുടിയേറുക}}, \emph{kuṭiyēṟuka}.) A send-off? (\textbf{\ml{യാത്രയയപ്പ്}}, \emph{yātrayayappŭ}.) To bid farewell? (\textbf{\ml{വിടവാങ്ങുക}}, \emph{viṭavāṅṅuka}.) To see off? (\textbf{\ml{യാത്രയാക്കുക}}, \emph{yātrayākkuka}.) To say goodbye? (\textbf{\ml{വിടപറയുക}}, \emph{viṭapaṟayuka}.) To leave one's homeland? (\textbf{\ml{നാടുവിടുക}}, \emph{nāṭuviṭuka}.) A funeral? (\textbf{\ml{ശവസംസ്കാരം}}, \emph{śavasaṁskāraṁ}.) A cremation ground? (\textbf{\ml{ശ്മശാനം}}, \emph{śmaśānaṁ}.) A coffin? (\textbf{\ml{ശവപ്പെട്ടി}}, \emph{śavappeṭṭi}.) To cremate? (\textbf{\ml{ദഹിപ്പിക്കുക}}, \emph{dahippikkuka}.) To bury? (\textbf{\ml{കുഴിച്ചിടുക}}, \emph{kuḻicciṭuka}.) Condolence? (\textbf{\ml{അനുശോചനം}}, \emph{anuśōcanaṁ}.) A tribute? (\textbf{\ml{ആദരാഞ്ജലി}}, \emph{ādarāñjali}.) A death anniversary? (\textbf{\ml{ചരമവാർഷികം}}, \emph{caramavārṣikaṁ}.) A cemetery? (\textbf{\ml{സെമിത്തേരി}}, \emph{semittēri}.) To offer condolences? (\textbf{\ml{അനുശോചിക്കുക}}, \emph{anuśōcikkuka}.) A commemoration? (\textbf{\ml{അനുസ്മരണം}}, \emph{anusmaraṇaṁ}.) A memorial? (\textbf{\ml{സ്മാരകം}}, \emph{smārakaṁ}.) A statue? (\textbf{\ml{പ്രതിമ}}, \emph{pratima}.) A stone inscription? (\textbf{\ml{ശിലാലിഖിതം}}, \emph{śilālikhitaṁ}.) To commemorate? (\textbf{\ml{അനുസ്മരിക്കുക}}, \emph{anusmarikkuka}.) Property? (\textbf{\ml{സ്വത്ത്}}, \emph{svattŭ}.) An heir? (\textbf{\ml{അവകാശി}}, \emph{avakāśi}.) A will? (\textbf{\ml{ഒസ്യത്ത്}}, \emph{osyattŭ}.) A widow? (\textbf{\ml{വിധവ}}, \emph{vidhava}.) Heritage? (\textbf{\ml{പൈതൃകം}}, \emph{paitṛkaṁ}.) An ancestor? (\textbf{\ml{പൂർവികൻ}}, \emph{pūrvikan}.) A successor? (\textbf{\ml{പിൻഗാമി}}, \emph{pingāmi}.) A custom? (\textbf{\ml{ആചാരം}}, \emph{ācāraṁ}.) An origin? (\textbf{\ml{ഉത്ഭവം}}, \emph{utbhavaṁ}.) A grandmother's tale? (\textbf{\ml{മുത്തശ്ശിക്കഥ}}, \emph{muttaśśikkatha}.) An award? (\textbf{\ml{പുരസ്കാരം}}, \emph{puraskāraṁ}.) An honour? (\textbf{\ml{ബഹുമതി}}, \emph{bahumati}.) A winner? (\textbf{\ml{ജേതാവ്}}, \emph{jētāvŭ}.) To honour? (\textbf{\ml{ആദരിക്കുക}}, \emph{ādarikkuka}.) To make one's own? (\textbf{\ml{സ്വന്തമാക്കുക}}, \emph{svantamākkuka}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
